ai.title: Fix agent usage command in first agent docs
ai.summary: Corrected `codebuff --agent` command syntax in `creating-your-first-agent.mdx`. Removed erroneous `@` prefix from publisher ID. Affects documentation only.

eli5.text: The step-by-step guide for creating your first assistant had a small typo in the example command for using someone else's assistant: it showed an extra @ symbol before the publisher name. That typo is now removed, so the command shown in the guide will actually work when you copy it. If you looked at the guide before, you may have tried the example and gotten an error; it now runs as written.

ai.title: Add Claude Sonnet 4.5 support and improve end-turn tool guidance
ai.summary: Added `anthropic/claude-4.5-sonnet` to OpenRouter model constants and provider order. Updated base agent definition and short model names to reference the new version. Improved `end-turn` tool description with explicit incorrect/correct usage examples. Enhanced error reporting in git evals judging failures.

eli5.text: If you've ever asked the assistant to hand control back to you, the instructions it follows now include a clear example of what not to do and what to do instead, so it stops returning tool calls that leave you hanging. The main assistant agents now use a newer model version behind the scenes, which means they can tap into improved reasoning and coding help when you chat with them. If you're running automated test comparisons of git changes, those test reports now show the actual error details when something fails, instead of just saying it broke. All of these updates are live today.

ai.title: base-max agent uses claude-sonnet-4.5
ai.summary: The `base-max` agent definition in `.agents/base-max.ts` now points to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` instead of `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`. This updates the underlying model for the max-tier base agent. No other files or surfaces are affected.

eli5.text: The most capable internal assistant tool now uses a newer, smarter AI model instead of the one it was using before. If you triggered that agent today, it would answer you using the new model without any change to how you interact with it. The change affects only that single high-tier agent and nothing else on the platform.

ai.title: Add cache control for OpenAI and Anthropic models
ai.summary: supportsCacheControl in common/src/old-constants.ts now returns true for any model ID starting with 'openai/' or 'anthropic/'. This enables cache control for all models under these namespaces, bypassing the previous explicit definition requirement. The change applies to the core shared constants, affecting all surfaces using this helper. Unknown models outside these prefixes continue to default to false.

eli5.text: If you use an assistant powered by certain OpenAI or Anthropic models, the assistant can now reuse earlier parts of your conversation instead of reprocessing them, which can make longer conversations faster and cheaper. This works automatically for any model whose name starts with those provider labels, without needing to set it up manually each time. If you use a different model family, nothing changes for you yet.

ai.title: Implementation planner agents switch to Claude 4.5 Sonnet
ai.summary: implementation-planner, implementation-planner-max, and plan-selector definitions updated from openai/gpt-5 to anthropic/claude-4.5-sonnet. reasoningOptions and thinker-gpt-5-high dependency removed from implementation-planner. Parallel spawn count for implementation-planner-max reduced from 10 to 5. GPT-5 specific tool-call enforcement prompt deleted.

eli5.text: The internal planning assistant that drafts code implementation plans now uses a different AI model (Sonnet 4.5) instead of GPT-5 for generating and selecting plans. If you watched the assistant work, you'd notice it spawns fewer parallel planning attempts (5 instead of 10) and no longer relies on GPT-5-specific reasoning settings, so its drafting process is restructured around the new model's capabilities. This affects anyone using the internal planning tools that chain together multiple planning agents before settling on a final implementation plan.

ai.title: Switch researcher and reviewer agents to Sonnet
ai.summary: Researcher and reviewer agents migrated from GPT-5 to `anthropic/claude-4.5-sonnet` to reduce latency and improve planning consistency. `base-max.ts` updates spawnable agent IDs to `researcher-web-sonnet` and `researcher-docs-sonnet`, while `reviewer-max.ts` switches the underlying model. `base-prompts.ts` enforces `implementation-planner-max` spawning for medium-to-hard tasks across all max-tier configurations.

eli5.text: Inside the company's internal tools, the team of automated 'researchers' and 'reviewers' that help build software has been quietly swapped from one AI brain to another (Claude's newer model). This was a behind-the-scenes change to make those helper agents run a bit faster and work more predictably, but it only affects how the company's engineers' tools behave, not anything an outside user would notice directly.

ai.title: Fix missing response content in AI SDK message table
ai.summary: Added `content += flushed` and `content += stopSequenceResult.text` in `promptAiSdkStream` (backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts). Accumulated yielded text-delta chunks into the `content` variable. Ensures full response text is captured for database persistence. Scope limited to Vercel AI SDK streaming handler.

eli5.text: When the assistant streams a reply in chunks, some of those chunks were not being added to the running record of what the assistant has said so far. As a result, the saved copy of the conversation could end up missing pieces of the assistant's response. The fix appends every streamed piece into that running record, so the full reply is stored correctly and nothing gets dropped from the saved message.

ai.title: Resolve escaped characters in image file paths
ai.summary: Added normalizeUserProvidedPath to decode Unicode, hex, and literal escapes in image paths before resolution. resolveFilePath now applies this normalization to handle tilde expansion, absolute checks, and relative resolution correctly. This affects npm-app/src/utils/image-handler.ts.

eli5.text: If you give the app an image path that contains encoded characters (like Unicode escapes, hex codes, or backslash sequences), the app now correctly translates those into the actual characters before finding your file. This means paths with special formatting from other systems will open properly instead of being treated as a different file or failing. This fix is live and applies to internal image handling for anyone uploading or referencing images through the app.

ai.title: Release 1.0.499 ships model and CLI updates
ai.summary: Version 1.0.499 is now published from npm-app/release/package.json, aggregating a day of changes across the Freebuff monorepo. This release adds Claude Sonnet 4.5 support to OpenRouter model constants and base agent definitions, switches GPT-5-dependent agents like implementation-planner and researcher to the new model, and introduces cache control for all openai/ and anthropic/ models via common/src/old-constants.ts. Additional notable changes include custom header support for remote MCP servers, new Notion query and researcher agents using x-ai/grok-4-fast, dynamic agent definition docs, and response content capture fixes in the Vercel AI SDK streaming handler.
ai.evidence: The only diff in this commit is a one-line version field change in npm-app/release/package.json, moving from "1.0.498" to "1.0.499". Analysis notes confirm the commit is solely a release-bump that aggregates multiple prior commits into the Freebuff repository, shipping features, model changes, and CLI improvements without modifying any other files in this commit.

eli5.text: This release updates the built-in AI assistants to use newer, faster models and adds new ways to connect to external tools and research information. You can now use the latest Claude 4.5 Sonnet and Grok models for your tasks, and the new Notion researcher agents can automatically gather information from your Notion pages by running multiple searches in parallel. Remote tool connections now support secure authentication headers, so you can safely link to private services, and the AI's responses are now saved fully and correctly in logs. Upgrading gives you faster, more accurate AI assistance, especially for planning and researching projects, along with better reliability when saving conversations and handling file paths.
